# How this series works

**30 Days of X** is a **series of independent volumes**, not one course you must take as a bundle. Each **volume** (sub-book) is a self-contained, expert-ordered path of roughly thirty intensive study days. You choose **which volume to follow** and **how to fit it into your life**.

## Relationship to 90 Days of X

This series is an **intensive condensation** of [90 Days of X](../../90DaysOfX/). Each 30-day chapter combines approximately three original 90-day chapters into a single comprehensive session. The same expert-curated ordering and gate system is preserved, but compressed into four stages of ~7 days each.

**Who this is for:**

- Learners who already have some programming/tech background and want faster pacing
- People revisiting material they've partially seen before
- Anyone who prefers intensive sprints over extended curricula

**Who should use 90DaysOfX instead:**

- Complete beginners who need more time to absorb each concept
- Learners who prefer a slower, more deliberate pace

## Core ideas

1. **Volumes are separate.** Finishing Go does not require NixOS (or any future volume), and the reverse is also true.  
2. **One volume at a time is the normal mode.** Studying two volumes in the same period is optional and entirely your decision—not a requirement of this resource.  
3. **Expert order inside each volume.** Day numbers are pacing guides; **gates** matter more than dates.  
4. **Syllabus first.** Narrative chapters are written against each volume's syllabus contract.  
5. **The series can grow.** A successful volume → add another without rewriting existing ones.  

## What a volume contains

| Piece | Purpose |
|-------|---------| 
| Overview | Audience, baseline versions, "done" criteria |
| Syllabus | 4 stages, 30 days, 4 gates, explicit out-of-scope |
| Chapters | Mental model → examples → labs → gotchas |

## Stage structure (every volume)

| Stage | Days | Role |
|-------|------|------|
| **Stage I** | 1–8 | Foundations — core concepts and first gate |
| **Stage II** | 9–15 | Intermediate — deeper skills and second gate |
| **Stage III** | 16–22 | Applied — real-world usage and third gate |
| **Stage IV** | 23–30 | Mastery & capstone — production polish and final gate |

## Quality bar (every volume)

- Prefer **official docs** over stale blogs when they conflict  
- **Ship artifacts** (repos, flakes, services), not only notes  
- End with a **capstone** that proves integration  
- No certification branding unless a volume deliberately adds exam prep later  

## Success for a single volume

You succeed when that volume's overview checklist and capstone hold—regardless of whether you ever open another volume in the series.
